questions.text: The Breadth First Search (BFS) algorithm has been implemented using the queue data structure. Which one of the following is a possible order of visiting the nodes in the graph below?
questions.solution:
BFS from P: neighbours O, Q; then O's new neighbour N, Q's new neighbour M; then M's new neighbour R [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] P O Q N M R True

The others break BFS order, e.g. MNOPQR visits O before Q and R, which are M's own neighbours.

Answer: POQNMR

questions.text: Match the algorithms with their time complexities:
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Towers of Hanoi: [latex]T(n)=2T(n-1)+1\Rightarrow\Theta(2^n)[/latex] (iii)
- Binary search: [latex]\Theta(\log n)[/latex] (iv)
- Heap sort worst case: [latex]\Theta(n\log n)[/latex] (ii)
- Adding two n [latex]\times[/latex] n matrices: [latex]n^2[/latex] additions, [latex]\Theta(n^2)[/latex] (i)

Answer: P-(iii), Q-(iv), R-(ii), S-(i)

questions.text:
Let G = (V, E) be any connected undirected edge-weighted graph. The weights of the edges in E are positive and distinct. Consider the following statements:

(I) Minimum spanning tree of G is always unique.
(II) Shortest path between any two vertices of G is always unique.

Which of the above statements is/are necessarily true?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- (I): distinct weights [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] unique MST True
- (II): two different paths can have equal total weight even with distinct edges (e.g. 1 + 4 = 2 + 3) False

Answer: (I) only

questions.text:
Consider the following table:

Match the algorithms to the design paradigms they are based on.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Kruskal: always picks the cheapest safe edge [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Greedy (ii)
- Quicksort: partition and recurse [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Divide and Conquer (i)
- Floyd-Warshall: builds on smaller subproblems [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Dynamic Programming (iii)

Answer: P-(ii), Q-(i), R-(iii)

questions.text:
Consider the following functions from positive integers to real numbers:

[latex]10,\sqrt{n},n, log_{2}n,\frac{100}{n}[/latex].

The CORRECT arrangement of the above functions in increasing order of asymptotic complexity is:
questions.solution:
100/n decreases to 0; 10 is constant; then [latex]\log_2 n \lt \sqrt n \lt n[/latex].

Answer: 100/n, 10, log2 n, √n, n
